bears_on: How are two different oracles at distance zero treated?
checked_examples.code:
theorem gap_le_one (o o' : Oracle) (n : ℕ) (y : Vector Bool n) :
    |(o n y).prob true - (o' n y).prob true| ≤ 1 := by
  have h0 := (o n y).prob_mem_Icc true
  have h1 := (o' n y).prob_mem_Icc true
  rw [abs_le]
  constructor <;> linarith [h0.1, h0.2, h1.1, h1.2]

theorem gap_le_dist (o o' : Oracle) (n : ℕ) (y : Vector Bool n) :
    |(o n y).prob true - (o' n y).prob true| ≤ dist o o' := by
  have inner : ∀ m, BddAbove (Set.range fun z : Vector Bool m => |(o m z).prob true - (o' m z).prob true|) := by
    intro m
    refine ⟨1, ?_⟩
    rintro _ ⟨z, rfl⟩
    exact gap_le_one o o' m z
  have outer : BddAbove (Set.range fun m => ⨆ z : Vector Bool m, |(o m z).prob true - (o' m z).prob true|) := by
    refine ⟨1, ?_⟩
    rintro _ ⟨m, rfl⟩
    letI : Nonempty (Vector Bool m) := ⟨Vector.replicate m false⟩
    exact ciSup_le fun z => gap_le_one o o' m z
  change _ ≤ ⨆ m, ⨆ z : Vector Bool m, |(o m z).prob true - (o' m z).prob true|
  exact le_trans (le_ciSup (inner n) y) (le_ciSup outer n)

theorem zero_distance_means_same_oracle (o o' : Oracle) (h : dist o o' = 0) : o = o' := by
  funext n y
  have hle := gap_le_dist o o' n y
  rw [h] at hle
  have htrue : (o n y).prob true = (o' n y).prob true :=
    sub_eq_zero.mp (abs_eq_zero.mp (le_antisymm hle (abs_nonneg _)))
  apply Prob.ext
  intro x
  cases x
  · rw [bool_prob_false_of_true, bool_prob_false_of_true, htrue]
  · exact htrue
checked_examples.says: two Lean oracles at distance zero are the same oracle
checked_examples.title: Distance zero means the same oracle

definition_quote.prose: In other words, if M is run with any oracle which assigns similar probabilities to 𝒪, the probability that M outputs 1 should change by at most a K factor more than the maximum difference in the oracle probabilities.
definition_quote.text: For K > 0, a probabilistic oracle machine M is K-Lipschitz at oracle 𝒪 if, for any other oracle 𝒪′, sup_x |P[M^𝒪(x) = 1] − P[M^𝒪′(x) = 1]| < K · sup_z |P[𝒪(z) = 1] − P[𝒪′(z) = 1]|.

lean_counterpart.code:
/-- An oracle computation is k-Lipschitz if the final probability differs by ≤ k * oracle dist.
    We define this asymmetrically, as we want the neighborhood of a particular oracle. -/
structure Oracle.lipschitz (o : Oracle) (t : ℕ) (k : ℝ) : Prop where
  k0 : 0 ≤ k
  le : ∀ o' : Oracle, |(o.final t).prob true - (o'.final t).prob true| ≤ k * dist o o'
lean_counterpart.summary: Lean uses ≤ instead of <, and compares the oracle with every formal oracle, including itself.

questions.why: If it does, both sides are zero and the strict < reads 0 < 0, which is false. No machine would then be K-Lipschitz, and Theorem 6.2 would apply to nothing. Lean's ≤ does not have this problem.

questions.question: Which governs: the displayed strict < or the prose “at most”?
questions.why: The prose describes ≤, which matches Lean. If ≤ governs, the strictness part of D01 goes away and only the comparison-domain difference (D02) is left. If < governs, whether 𝒪′ includes 𝒪 decides whether the definition can be met at all.
